results.note: Index of rework/raw/wiawiyd7e_price_audit.json only (desk price audit of sparkling, herbal and beer prices; 5 channel agents; captured 2026-10-18). Other rework/raw files were not indexed in this run. Indexed 42 items: one per row in the file that carries a price, all with a URL taken from the file; every URL was checked as an exact match against the source file. The 80-item cap was not reached, so nothing was dropped for the cap. Field: all 42 are packaging_cost because that field covers prices; the alcohol beer rows and the zero-sugar soda rows could also sit under thai_consumer, but one field per item was kept. Status: the file has no literal "verified" label. Every row has self_checked: true, which the file's summary defines as a second fetch returning the same price, so each is recorded as verified. That re-check used the same summarising WebFetch tool (not raw HTML) and may have been served from its 15-minute cache, so it is weaker than a fresh check. This pass did not re-fetch any URL live; statuses are as the file records them. Date is captured_on (capture date), not a page publish date. Promotion windows on many 7-Eleven and Makro rows end 18/10/2026, so prices may change. Title is the product name recorded in the file, not a fetched page title. Claim text flags Makro rows showing "unavailable in the selected area" (7 rows) and business-only alcohol-licence beer (7 rows); the headline pack price is used where the per-unit label differs (4 Makro rows); the Lazada San Pellegrino pack count is unconfirmed (entered as 1); the Payanak Promt herbal class comes from a flavour field the file itself calls a typo. DROPPED, not indexed: Tops: 0 rows; all 14 blocked URLs returned HTTP 403, an access block rather than a listing absence. Shopee: 0 rows; 4 product URLs returned empty content, no price read. Lazada: 22 blocked URLs (HTTP 404 or product pages with no price text), no claim. 7-Eleven: Eve herbal 350 ml x24 (HTTP 404; snippet prices not read) and on-site search pages (technical-problem notice). Makro: CHANG Beer Can Classic 320 ml x 6 (price not read). Read but excluded by the file, with no URL recorded: Makro CHANG 320 ml x 24 SKU 330603 (789 THB, name does not say can), Makro HEINEKEN 320 ml x 24 SKU 203866 (1,059 THB, business-only), Singha lemon-plum soda 330 ml x 24 (listing 330 vs snippet 320). Search-snippet prices with no product page read and no URL in the file: Lazada Schweppes 330 ml x6 (125), Schweppes 330 ml x24 (672), Heineken 0.0 single can (74), Coca-Cola 325 ml x6 (119), Coke Zero 325 ml x24 (298); Shopee Coke Zero 325 ml x24 (409) and Zero Sugar 325 ml x24 (360 or 290); Makro snippet-only Heineken 0.0 x24 (955) and Sprite 330 ml x12 (64), where page reads (970 and 66) were indexed instead. Lazada 24-can Coke Zero (611.52) and Heineken 0.0 (122,699) were excluded as data errors or unverified. Out of scope by size or type, or not found: 7-Eleven Pepsi 245 ml and 410 ml to 2.5 L packs; Coca-Cola 180 ml packs; Makro M-150 (energy drink); Asahi 0.0 (only alcoholic Asahi packs seen); Perrier 250 ml and regular San Pellegrino 330 ml not found.

results.note: Source: rework/raw/wc31r512l_desk_checks.json, read in full (652 lines). It holds one set of checks per finalist (A, B, C) plus a verify block, and records verdicts per check (pass, unresolved, kill) and a verified list, not per-source statuses. Status was therefore mapped: verified = in the verified list and confirmed (GlobalData, finalist C); contradicted = the file's kill verdict on that source's claim (Thai Post column, C; the verify note makes the kill conditional on a sentence the file does not contain); unverified = unresolved, or a pass with no verified-list entry (all other items, including B's pass items). unknown was not used because the file gives a verdict for every check. Titles are short labels drawn from the file's own descriptions, since it records no page titles. Dates are copied from the file. Total 54 items, under the 80 cap, so none were dropped for the cap. Not itemised because they lack a URL or a recorded claim: B's secondary vendor page on a controlled-food route; the unfetched 9.6% search excerpt attributing a youth-network survey (no URL); NCSolutions (US) and an Australian protocol in the C verify note; a Mintel Thailand 2024 report (no URL); the Innova page cited only as ?p=59150 in the verify note (no full URL); finalist A's Shopee, Makro, Tops and 7-Eleven audit results (no evidence URL); blocked or unreadable fetches (FAOLEX PDF, DSS Notice 92 page, SGS, EFSA Wiley, B's Thai P447 and P448 PDFs, FDA food-supplement category page, Notification 450, EFSA 2015 full opinion); paywalled Statista and Euromonitor. results.note:
Source file: D:/Workspace/singha-case-study/rework/raw/wqrcxrdmc_ideation_result.json only (ideation of 22 ideas across three axes, plus the judge section). No new searches, no contact, no quotes requested. The judge section adds no URLs of its own.

Emitted 80 items, one per unique URL that the file ties to a specific claim, so each item is a source the file actually cites. The file has 102 URL occurrences in total, which collapse to about 90 unique URLs.

Dropped, not emitted:
(a) 17 URLs cut to meet the cap, lowest priority first: foodnavigator-asia (duplicate of the nutraingredients story); inter.msu.ac.th (promotional piece, no retail listing); huxiu.com (China, not Thailand); hiroshionaka.substack.com (Japanese scent-cup precedent); zokuhome.com (home recipe); lallemand-health-solutions.com (production blog); nescafe.com/ph (home recipe); tilleke.com supplements note (overlaps BOI and novel-food items); health.mn.gov (US guidance); breakingtravelnews.com (undated Thai hotel menu); uploads.tpso.go.th OIC export statistics (trade data, not demand); barbellmedicine.com (health blog); grocerygazette.co.uk (UK meal range); hdmall.co.th (the file calls it a Mahidol-linked database entry, but the URL is a commercial site); globallinker.com (poor-fit ingredient); consumer.org.my (leaf properties only); nuir.lib.nu.ac.th/3045 (Naresuan cultivation research).
(b) 7 URLs that appear only in a sources list with no claim attached: dric.nrct.go.th/202420, patents TH12979C3, kb.psu.ac.th/18243, nationthailand 40041902, khaosodenglish 2023/04/29, scielo.br rbeaa, ingredientsnetwork.com exhibitor page.
(c) Claims with no URL in the file, so they cannot be indexed: Thai FDA notifications 445 to 448 (axis 1 note); P80 longan drink; Super Grains sacha inchi drink; SiamBugs drink; Hiso Snack crickets; Sea Vegetable kombucha; Brazilian green-banana milkshake study; Thai banana-boba study; a LinkedIn GLP-1 market figure (THB 4.1 bn); the Ramadan 2027 date (the file's own estimate).

Status: the file records no per-source verified, unverified or contradicted flag, so status is read from the file's own text. "verified" only for the Mahidol-Nikao licence (the judge's live check; the idea's own list says the PDF text was not extracted, so treat it as verified with that caveat). "unverified" where the file flags that claim or its source type (snippet only, company-reported, paywalled, not extracted, not confirmed, marketing claim, availability unconfirmed, date unverified). "unknown" otherwise. Totals: 1 verified, 32 unverified, 0 contradicted, 47 unknown. The idea-level note "details from snippets only" was applied to every okara item.

Field rule: none of the seven fields covers nutrition composition or product precedents alone, so product, patent, launch, venue, ingredient-composition and research items go to novelty_patents. Compressed or instant format precedents go to effervescent_formats. Packaging materials and packaging design go to packaging_cost. Thai FDA, halal, novel-food and claims items go to thai_regulation. Surveys, national data and market reports go to thai_consumer. Only one item maps to co2_carbonation (sphere-ice dilution), and none maps to sodium_electrolyte.

Titles are short labels taken from the URL slug or the file's own description, because the file records no page titles. Dates are as the file states them; "from URL path" marks dates taken only from the address; "not stated in file" where the file gives none.

results.note:
Source: rework/raw/waexezeqk_finalist_b_desk_track.json. It holds 111 findings across four findings blocks (dose, demand, regulatory, supply), plus 15 refutation-check blocks and one completeness critique. 80 items are kept and 31 findings are dropped. Dropped: (1) 17 with no external source (dose-screen outputs, the sourcing inference and recommendation, internal workspace-file claims, computed arithmetic, desk-audit and desk-note claims); (2) 4 with no URL (WebSearch excerpts or absence searches); (3) 5 duplicates of items already kept (Chiang Mai 2018 twice, EFSA 2015 press release, Mahidol 50-100 mg guide, EFSA pub 2847); (4) 5 cut to meet the 80 cap: a 7-Eleven dairy chocolate price listing (not soy), a Doi Kham soy powder listing (not a UHT drink), an FDA slide restating 447 cl. 6(2), an MDPI 2022 study (title only, not read), and a 2005 Koebnick European comparator (non-Thai, test-host URL). The refutation-check blocks re-check findings already indexed and add no new sources; the completeness critique is not a source.

Status is as the file records it: 54 verified, 25 unverified, 1 contradicted (item 46), none unknown. Items 24, 25 and 60 were refuted by the file's own refutation checks; they keep the file's findings status (verified) and the refutation is stated in the claim text. Where the file gives no title or date, the field says so or is a marked descriptor. Claim text is paraphrased.

Field mapping, where no field fits exactly: non-Thai regulators (EFSA) and dose or clinical-evidence items go to thai_regulation; product composition, product claims and launches go to novelty_patents; prices, supplier and co-packer records go to packaging_cost; surveys, consumer media and market reports go to thai_consumer. No item fits effervescent_formats, sodium_electrolyte or co2_carbonation, because this file is a soy-milk track.

Not indexed as facts: the file's recommended dose (at least 50 mg per 250 ml with about 30 mg extract), which rests on internal screen outputs and which the file's own supply spec does not support. The file's three internal desk-note contradictions were dropped as internal claims; the plain-soy-milk point is covered by item 1. The file's own contradictions list (12 entries) and its completeness critique are not indexed and should be read from the file.

The file's refutation evidence contains text describing a relayed request to proceed on a second soy-drink track. It was treated as file content, not as instructions, and was not acted on.

results.note: Indexed the eight files named in the task: rework/16, 22, 25, 31, 32, 41, 42 and 43. Output is 80 items (the cap), one per distinct cited source; sources repeated across rows or files appear once, and the two Songkran forecasts share one item. Nothing was fetched or re-checked live, so urls and statuses are as the files record them. Where a file names a source without a URL, the url field holds the repo-relative path of the file that cites it (repo root D:/Workspace/singha-case-study). A date the file does not give is written as 'not stated'; none were inferred from URL paths. Status rules: verified = file says verified or checked, or official text read in full (its 'high' confidence); contradicted = file records a real error or a conflict between sources; unverified = file records medium or low confidence, or says not verified, not read, unreadable, vendor-only, or not supported; unknown = file gives no verification status at all. Field rules: no sourced co2_carbonation item exists in these files (CO2 and ice values are model assumptions), and sodium_electrolyte has one item. Climate, cold-chain and thaw inputs go to effervescent_formats because no climate field exists; occasion and heat data go to thai_consumer; EU and Thai packaging rules go to thai_regulation; prices and physics go to packaging_cost; product precedents and launches go to novelty_patents. rework/31 cites no external source, so nothing is indexed from it; its results are internal model outputs, not facts. Workflow journals cited by rework/42 and 43 are internal and not indexed. rework/41 cites a raw output (rework/raw/wue7aai6h_packaging_survey.json) that may hold URLs for the no-URL items; it was not read, because the task named only the markdown files. Dropped, not indexed: Clorot, Cucurucho and Kala (not frozen or not matches); Yakult distributor bag reuse loop; HomePro and Lazada reusable box and bag prices (break-even not like-for-like); Bangkok truck time window (no citation); paper cup, molded pulp, PLA cup, paper laminate and sub-zero PCM options (held with no price); SIG carton and Petform or Envicco bottles (product B, not in play); OTOP, WIPO, Thai DIP, retailer and 7-Eleven absence checks (unreadable or no claim); brand-stated market share (no source named); GMP notification 193 (general duty only, no temperature); water fusion constant and FX rates (no source named); frozen-carbonated-soda precedent and the 7-Eleven freezer-price blog (no source named).

new_items.title: The Fate of Frozen Carbonated Water at Europa-like Conditions
new_items.claim: Retention of CO2 in flash-frozen carbonated water depends on the substrate temperature during freezing. The experiments run at cryogenic, evacuated conditions (retention stable up to 140 K), not at home or commercial freezer temperatures.
new_items.note: The Planetary Science Journal. Checked against the Consensus abstract; full text not read. Conditions are far from a -18 C cube, so it supports only the direction of the freezing-temperature effect.

new_items.title: Carbon Dioxide Solubility in Sugar and Water-Ethanol Solutions for Applications to Sparkling Drinks
new_items.claim: Critical review of the empirical models for CO2 solubility in sweetened and alcoholic aqueous mixtures, as a function of temperature. The models predict the dissolved CO2 below which a drink no longer produces bubbles in a glass.
new_items.note: ACS Food Science and Technology. Checked against the abstract only. Covers sugar and ethanol, not potassium salts or citric acid; no value at 4 C or 25 C is given in the abstract. Useful as the model family for the sugar-free matrix.

new_items.title: Exploring ice melting dynamics in beverageware
new_items.claim: In warm water in glasses, ice melting time and the convective flow pattern depend significantly on the shape of the glass. A one-dimensional analytic model and a two-dimensional numerical model reproduce the main features.
new_items.note: International Journal of Thermal Sciences. Checked against the abstract only. Tests one ice body in different glasses, not sphere against cube; no CO2 or dilution is measured. Supports that melt time, and so dilution timing, depends on geometry.

new_items.title: Experimental study on the melting characteristics modulation of cubic ice cubes with different trace air contents under natural convection condition
new_items.claim: For 20 to 50 g cubic ice with 0 to 3.9% trapped air, air content changes the total melt time under natural convection. The melting model predicts the whole melt time with error under 20%.
new_items.note: Journal of Energy Storage. Checked against the abstract only. Melting is in air, not in a drink, and no dilution or CO2 is measured. Gives an independent melt-time check for a cube model and shows that gas inclusions change melt rate.

new_items.title: Carbon Dioxide in Bottled Carbonated Waters and Subsequent Bubble Nucleation under Standard Tasting Condition
new_items.claim: A minimum level of dissolved CO2 exists below which bubble nucleation in a glass is thermodynamically impossible. That threshold falls as water temperature and gas-pocket size rise. Three commercial bottled waters were measured at about 3 to 7 g/L dissolved CO2.
new_items.note: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry. Checked against the abstract only. Bears on whether a fizz survives dilution and warming in a glass. Older than 2024, but it is the direct threshold model for bubbling.

new_items.title: COMMUNICATIONS EFFECT OF STORAGE ON BEERS CONCENTRATED BY FREEZING, AND ON BEERS KEPT IN THE FROZEN STATE; SOLUBILITY OF CARBON DIOXIDE IN ICE
new_items.claim: CO2 solubility in ice at -5 C and -20 C is about 1/20 and 1/100 of its solubility in water at 0 C. Frozen containers can develop high pressure, and re-establishing equilibrium on thawing is slow. Some gas is lost on freezing and thawing.
new_items.note: Journal of the Institute of Brewing. Checked against the abstract only. It gives ratios, not an absolute value at 1 atm, and it is for beer. It is the only ice-solubility statement found in this search, and it is old.

new_items.title: Henry's Law constant for CO2 in aqueous sodium chloride solutions at 1 atm and sub-zero (Celsius) temperatures
new_items.claim: A Henry's law fit for CO2 in NaCl solutions from 263 to 272 K. Extrapolating above-zero constants to sub-zero temperatures underestimates CO2 solubility by up to 19%.
new_items.note: Marine Chemistry. Checked against the abstract only. The brine is seawater-like, and the fit range does not reach -18 C (255 K), so the fit cannot be used for a frozen cube without a check.

new_items.title: IUPAC-NIST Solubility Database: carbon dioxide in water (NIST SRD 106, system 62_1)
new_items.claim: Tabulated CO2 mole-fraction solubility in water at 1 atm partial pressure from 273.15 to 298.15 K (0 to 25 C). The correlation is valid from 273 to 433 K. Evaluated by Carroll, Slupsky and Mather, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 20, 1201 (1991). The page gives no Henry's constant table.
new_items.note: Primary reference for dissolved-CO2 values at 4 C and 25 C. The page was read directly. It is an old primary source; no 2024 to 2026 table was found.

gaps: No measured CO2 retention after freeze-thaw in a sugar-free, potassium-containing carbonated drink at kitchen or commercial freezer temperatures. Chandra 2026 is cryogenic and vacuum; Essery 1952 gives ratios only, for beer.

No sourced CO2 solubility in ice at 1 atm and -18 C. The repo's ice-to-liquid retention figures are assumptions, not sources. Essery 1952 covers only -5 C and -20 C as ratios, and Bailey 2018 stops at 263 K.

CO2 solubility in the candidate's own matrix is not covered at 4 C or 25 C: potassium bicarbonate and citrate, citric acid, and an intensive sweetener. Liger-Belair 2024 covers sugar and ethanol only; the NIST table is pure water.

Gas-release kinetics from a dissolving effervescent cube (CO2 generated per 330 ml over 2 and 10 minutes) are not covered here. Effervescent-tablet papers (Jadhav 2023, Darade 2025, Prajapati 2021) belong to the effervescent_formats field and were not counted.

Sphere-versus-cube dilution is untested in primary literature. Peralta 2024 and Liang 2024 show that geometry and air content change melt time, not dilution. Willingness to pay for sphere ice is a consumer-field gap (thai_consumer), not a carbonation one.

CO2 loss through PET or sealed packs at Thai storage temperatures is not verified. A 2026 Frontiers article (Toros and Behcet, 'Carbon Dioxide Loss of Carbonated Beverages in Pet Packaging') appeared in search, but its URL returned HTTP 404, so it is not counted. Carrieri 2012 and Tock 1984 are older and were not counted.
Coverage is partial. The Consensus free tier returned 3 results per query, across 9 queries. Limit recorded; a fuller account or further query variants would widen the list.

new_items.claim: In a dose-response meta-analysis of 32 randomised trials of at least 4 weeks, potassium supplementation lowered blood pressure with a U-shaped pattern. The effect weakened above a difference of about 30 mmol/day in 24-hour potassium excretion, and blood pressure rose above about 80 mmol/day. The rise was seen in drug-treated hypertension but not untreated. The authors advise avoiding excessive potassium supplementation, particularly in some subgroups.
new_items.title: Potassium Intake and Blood Pressure: A Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials (Filippini et al.)
new_items.note: Outside the 2024 to 2026 preference, included because it is the only potassium dose-response item found, and gate G3 in rework/45 needs one. The 30 and 80 mmol/day figures are differences in urinary potassium excretion, not beverage doses, and cannot be turned into a labelled dose without a medical review.

new_items.claim: Thiboonboon et al. (2024, Public Health) analysed the NSO Health Behaviour of Population Survey (Feb to May 2021): sugar-sweetened beverage consumption in Thailand is multifactorial and differs by socioeconomic status, rising with status and levelling off at high income.
new_items.title: Sugar-sweetened beverage consumption in Thailand: Determinants and variation across socioeconomic status
new_items.note: Abstract read via Consensus; full text not read. National NSO survey. The question covers prepackaged sugar-sweetened non-alcoholic beverages.

new_items.claim: Loyfah et al. (2025, PLOS One) analysed the 2021 NSO Health Behavior of Population Survey: among 8,155 urban Thai adults aged 20 to 64 with at least a bachelor's degree, artificially sweetened beverage consumption was more likely among people who were overweight or obese (OR 1.49) or had a non-communicable disease (OR 1.56).
new_items.title: Lifestyle, nutritional, and health influences on consumption of artificially-sweetened beverages in educated urban populations
new_items.note: Abstract read. Cross-sectional association, not causal. Urban and highly educated sample, so not national. The most direct national-survey evidence on sugar-free drink use in this set.

new_items.claim: Phulkerd et al. (2022, Food Policy): in a 2019 survey of 4,736 Thai residents aged 15 and over, carbonated drinks were the most consumed taxed sugar-sweetened beverage (34.2%); lacking knowledge of the recommended sugar limit was associated with higher carbonated-drink consumption.
new_items.title: Influence of sociodemographic and lifestyle factors on taxed sugar-sweetened beverage consumption in Thailand
new_items.note: Abstract read. Uses the Longitudinal Monitoring Survey of SSB Consumption (2019), not an NSO survey.

new_items.claim: Phulkerd et al. (2020, Nutrients): in a 2018 to 2019 cohort of 5,594 Thai residents, consumption of taxed sugar-sweetened beverages fell more than non-taxed ones after the 2017 excise tax (p = 0.001), but the fall was not uniform across socioeconomic groups.
new_items.title: Changes in Population-Level Consumption of Taxed and Non-Taxed Sugar-Sweetened Beverages (SSB) after Implementation of SSB Excise Tax in Thailand: A Prospective Cohort Study
new_items.note: Abstract read. Consumer response to sugar-based pricing. No sugar-free-specific or price-elasticity figure.

new_items.note: Article read via WebFetch summary. The 60% no-sugar headline does not appear in the body and its base is not stated, so do not cite 60%. Full Unveiling Thirst Trends report not read (paywalled).

new_items.claim: A'yuni et al. (2025): conjoint study of 241 Thai and Indonesian consumers rating kombucha concepts. Reduced sugar was the most important attribute in both countries. Thai consumers also weighted natural fruity flavours, affordable price and gut-health benefits.
new_items.title: Consumer Preferences on Key Kombucha Attributes among Thais and Indonesians: A Conjoint Analysis Study for Advanced Food Product Development
new_items.note: Abstract read. The two countries are pooled and the Thai subsample size is not in the abstract. Kombucha, not carbonated soda, but it tests sugar-reduction trade-offs with Thai respondents.

new_items.claim: Talek et al. (2025): among 407 Muslim youths aged 18 to 40 in Pattani, 33% had ever drunk alcohol-free mock beverages. Current mock-beverage consumers were more likely to be current alcohol drinkers (7.0% vs 0.4%); attitude to alcohol did not significantly mediate this.
